content.text:
**Finding submitted — deviation (T4C), fallback target.**

**What the document says.** The only convenience machinery is Section 4.1 (p0024): a one-year term auto-renewing each anniversary "unless terminated by either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other." Section 1.6 (p0011) is a cause right (Site not operational), not convenience, so it doesn't bear on this rule.

**Classification.** Three of four fallback elements are already met on their material terms:
- Customer notice sits at 90 days, inside the 60–90 day band;
- HDI's right operates only against the annual renewal, i.e. at the end of a term;
- HDI must give 90 days' notice.

The fallback fails on the fee element. Section 4.2(a) (p0026) imposes a Termination Payment of half of twelve months' Net Sales less $800,000 on *any* Company termination, uncapped, payable over eight quarters under 4.2(c). That is a materially punitive exit charge, not a capped early-termination fee.

**The edit.** One insertion after p0029 as new 4.2(d), capping the Termination Payment at three months of the Section 3.1 payments. I did not upgrade to preferred (30 days, no HDI convenience right, pro-rata refund), because the existing mutual 90-day end-of-term structure already satisfies the fallback and deleting HDI's right would require collateral rewrites of the renewal mechanic; the shorter notice and refund are noted in the rationale rather than pressed.
